For the automatic evaluation in the supervised setting, following the prior work, we assess the performance of the models based on: (1) Style Strength (ACC): The binary style classifier TexCNN (with 87.0% and 89.3% accuracy on E&M and F&R domains, respectively) is employed to predict the strength of the style conversion; (2) Content Preservation (BLEU): The BLEU score computed using four reference sentences; (3) HM: The harmonic mean of ACC and BLEU; and (4) BLEURT: A new metric for content preservation proposed by . For the automatic evaluation in the unsupervised setting, following prior work, we use: (1) Style Transfer Accuracy (S-ACC)... (2) Content Preservation (self-BLEU, ref-BLEU, BERT-P, BERT-R, and BERT-F1)... (3) Fluency (PPL)...

For human evaluation, following prior work, we randomly select 150 documents for each test set and we hire 4 annotators to rate model predictions from 1 (Very Bad) to 5 (Very Good) on content preservation, style conversion, and fluency.
